sections.h2: How do I sell my house fast in Burleson, TX?
sections.html:
Burleson owners can choose a listing, a sale without an agent, or a direct cash purchase. Burleson sellers who need speed usually weigh a cash offer against the cost of repairs and the weeks a listing can sit. Get the offer in writing and ask what happens to the price after the buyer's inspection.

Burleson is a growing suburb south of Fort Worth, and its buyer pool includes commuters, families and investors working the southern edge of the Dallas-Fort Worth area. Because the city crosses a county line, start by confirming which county your parcel is in, since that decides where the deed is recorded and who bills the tax.

sections.h2: Where is Burleson and what is the town like?
sections.html:
Burleson sits on the southern edge of the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex and spans both Johnson and Tarrant counties. The FY27 adopted budget profile lists 29.6 square miles, more than 55,000 residents, a median age of 36.9, a 3.1 percent unemployment rate and per capita income of $45,663, drawing on Esri, the Census Bureau and the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

  • Interstate 35W runs through town, about 15 miles south of downtown Fort Worth and 40 miles southwest of Dallas.
  • FM 1187 and SH 174 add other routes, and four airports sit nearby, including DFW International and Fort Worth Spinks.
  • The budget lists manufacturing, logistics, distribution, healthcare and retail among the local employers.
  • The city counts more than 20 parks and a Historic Old Town as community anchors.

Newer subdivisions and older homes near Old Town can price very differently, so ask any buyer which comparables they used.

sections.h2: What is Burleson's history, and why does it matter for older houses?
sections.html:
The town began in 1881 when the Missouri, Kansas and Texas railroad arrived, and it was incorporated in 1912, according to the city budget profile. Johnson County's museum page adds that an earlier settlement called Brushy Mound was bypassed by the railroad, that the post office opened in 1882, and that the town got an interurban stop in 1912 and electricity in 1913.

Cotton drove the early economy, and the population was only a few hundred for decades. Most of what exists today was built in the growth years since, but houses near the original townsite can be a century old. Older houses often need updated electrical panels, galvanized plumbing replaced and slabs or piers checked, so expect a buyer to price those items.

sections.h2: Can I rent my Burleson house short term before selling?
sections.html:
Burleson requires a permit. Under Chapter 14, Article XII of the city code, a short-term rental is a residence used for lodging for not less than one and not more than thirty consecutive days, and operating one without a permit is unlawful. The rules matter to a seller because an active permit does not transfer.

Burleson short-term rental permit rules, from the city code
TopicRule
Permit termExpires on the last day of the month one year after issue
Renewal filingOpens 30 days before expiration
InspectionOn-site, within 10 days of notice from the city
Changes to the applicationReported within 10 days
Fine, no culpable mental stateUp to $500
Fine, fire safety or public health offense with a culpable mental stateUp to $2,000

Source: City of Burleson code, Short-Term Rental Registration. The same article says the permit is not transferable, so a buyer who wants to operate a rental has to apply on their own. It also gives an affirmative defense when an occupant is a party to the sale and stays under a written post-closing occupancy agreement.

sections.h2: How do Burleson property taxes and exemptions work?
sections.html:
The appraisal district for the county where your parcel sits sets the value each January 1, and the taxing units set rates later in the year. Texas has no state property tax. Taxes for a year are due on receipt of the October bill, with the Comptroller saying most must be paid by January 31 to avoid a February 1 delinquency.

  • Late payment adds six percent penalty and one percent interest in February, and the penalty keeps rising through July 1.
  • A lawyer hired by the unit can add up to 20 percent more.
  • Homeowners may split the bill, with half due by November 30 and half by June 30.
  • Homeowners past 65 or with a disability may choose four installments.

Ask the Johnson County or Tarrant County tax office, whichever bills your parcel, for the exact payoff before closing.

sections.h2: What happens if a Burleson owner is behind on the mortgage?
sections.html:
Texas foreclosure is usually non-judicial, handled under the power of sale in the deed of trust. A servicer sends a default notice, allows 20 days to catch up, and then sends a notice of sale at least 21 days before the auction. The notice is posted at the courthouse and filed with the county clerk. For a house in Johnson County or Tarrant County, check that county's clerk for the posted notice.

Sales are held on the first Tuesday of the month, starting at the stated time and no more than three hours later. If the sale price does not cover the debt, the lender has two years to sue for a deficiency, and the borrower can ask for a fair market value offset. Selling ahead of the date usually costs less than letting the house go to auction.

sections.h2: What should I do about tenants in a Burleson house I want to sell?
sections.html:
A landlord generally gives at least three days' written notice to vacate unless the lease says otherwise, then files a suit in justice court. The hearing is set between 10 and 21 days after filing, and a tenant can appeal to county court within five days of judgment.

After the appeal window, a writ of possession can issue six days after final judgment and cannot issue more than 60 days after judgment unless the court allows longer. If a cash buyer purchases the house with the tenant in place, ask that the contract spell out who owns the lease and the deposit.

sections.h2: What if Burleson taxes are already late or the value looks too high?
sections.html:
Late taxes can still be managed. The Comptroller says a collector may allow a payment plan of up to 36 months on delinquent tax, and the plan is required for a residence homestead. A request to waive penalty and interest generally has to be made in writing before the 181st day after the delinquency date, and the tax itself usually has to be paid by the 21st day after the owner learns of the delinquency.

  • A value you dispute goes first to the appraisal review board, around the May 15 protest deadline.
  • After that ruling, an owner can go to district court, to binding arbitration, or to the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the board value is over $1,000,000.
  • An owner who appeals should still pay the undisputed tax before the delinquency date.
  • Unpaid tax follows the land because the lien attaches on January 1, so any buyer will want it cleared.

Bring the notice of appraised value and your latest bill to any sale conversation, since both show a buyer what the carrying cost will be.

faqs.q: Is Burleson in Johnson County or Tarrant County?
faqs.a: Both. The city spans Johnson and Tarrant counties, so your parcel's county decides the clerk, appraisal district and tax office. Check your tax statement or county map before you order title work.

faqs.q: Can a buyer keep my Burleson short-term rental permit?
faqs.a: No. The city code says a permit is not transferable and cannot be assigned. A new owner who wants to rent short term must apply for a permit and pass the on-site inspection.

faqs.q: How much penalty applies to late Burleson property tax?
faqs.a: Six percent penalty and one percent interest attach on February 1, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1. Interest keeps running at one percent a month. A collection lawyer can add up to 20 percent, so pay or arrange a plan early.

faqs.q: How long does a Texas foreclosure take once a notice is sent?
faqs.a: After the default notice, the borrower has 20 days to reinstate, and the notice of sale must come at least 21 days before the first-Tuesday auction. That is the minimum timeline, so a sale can be arranged within it.

faqs.q: What fine applies to an unpermitted Burleson short-term rental?
faqs.a: A violation without a culpable mental state is a Class C misdemeanor with a fine of up to $500. A fire-safety or public-health offense charged with a culpable mental state can carry a fine up to $2,000. Fees and rules can change, so ask the city for the current schedule.
